---
title: "3 · Open questions"
---

::: milestone
**If you're ahead**, you can explore the following questions. Not everything here has a known answer.
:::

## 1 · The matcher goes quiet

In the pair corpus, filter `role == "matcher"` and track their messages per repetition: how many, and how many containing `"\\?"`. They nearly vanish by round six. So who built the shorthand: the one who shortened, or the one who stopped needing to ask? And in the multiparty data the matchers *couldn't* all ask: is that exactly why the crowds stayed wordy?

## 2 · Do crowds invent different names?

Pair-built names got weird: *mouse*, *angel praying*. A name for five people has to work for five first-impressions at once. Pull round-6 descriptions for one tangram from the 2-player and the 6-player groups and read them side by side: are crowd names more literal? More *square-triangle-head*? Less *mouse*?


## 3 · Does shorthand transfer?

Pair 11's *mouse* would baffle pair 10. But a matcher from a 6-player group has heard descriptions built for a crowd. Would *they* fare better with a stranger's names? Wilkes-Gibbs & Clark (1992) swapped listeners mid-game to test this in pairs; design the group version: measure, prediction, and the result that would surprise you.

## 4 · Invent the measure

Hedges vanished in pairs. Pick something else that marks *not-yet-knowing-together*: pointing language (*this one*), questions from the describer, politeness, and track it in **both** datasets: does it fade faster with one matcher than with five?
